case_name: Smt. Ram Pyari vs Dharam Das And Ors.

parties.respondent_defendant: Dharam Das And Ors. (kith and kin of Tula Ram)

facts_of_case: Smt. Ram Pyari moved an application for grant of a succession certificate before the District Judge, Kumaun to the assets of her husband Tula Ram. The objectors pleaded that Smt. Ram Pyari was not the legally wedded wife of Tula Ram and she was not entitled to the grant of the succession certificate.

legal_principles.principle: A person affected by an illegal marriage can file a suit in the Civil Court for its declaration as void.
legal_principles.held: There is inherent right in every person to bring a suit of a civil nature and unless the suit is barred by statute, one may at one's peril bring a suit of one's choice.
cited_cases: Ganga Bai v. Vijai Kumar (AIR 1974 SC 1126)

legal_principles.principle: A stranger whose interest is affected by a null and void marriage can seek his remedy under the general law.
legal_principles.held: a marriage which is null and void may be declared to be so even at the instance of a stranger whose interest is affected by such marriage.
cited_cases: T. Rangaswami v. T. Aravindammal (AIR 1957 Mad 243)

use_for_drafting: representing third party interests in family disputes
